questions.hint: Follow stored deformation through recovery, formation of new grains, and later coarsening.
questions.explanation: Annealing commonly proceeds through recovery, recrystallization and grain growth. Recovery rearranges or removes defects; recrystallization replaces deformed material with new low-dislocation grains; subsequent growth increases average grain size. Strength usually falls and ductility recovers relative to the cold-worked condition. Recrystallization temperatures are often about 0.3–0.6 Tm, using absolute kelvin temperatures.

Mass fractions follow the lever rule: wα = (Cβ−C₀)/(Cβ−Cα), wβ = (C₀−Cα)/(Cβ−Cα), and sum to one. Above the liquidus everything is liquid; below the solidus everything is solid. Phase identity, phase composition and phase amount are different outputs.

Alpha is Pb-rich and beta Sn-rich. A hypoeutectic alloy forms primary alpha before the remaining liquid becomes eutectic; a hypereutectic alloy forms primary beta. At the eutectic composition, the solid can be an alternating alpha/beta lamellar mixture.

Carbon diffusion allows the carbon-poor ferrite and carbon-rich carbide to develop.

Carbon is trapped, producing the body-centered-tetragonal structure in carbon steel rather than equilibrium ferrite plus carbide. Carbon increases the distortion and generally raises hardness. The martensite fraction depends strongly on the lowest temperature reached. Tempering subsequently lets carbon redistribute and usually trades some hardness for improved toughness.
